# Lucas Arana

> Lucas Arana is Chief Operating Officer (COO) at Nexton, a staffing company that builds and runs remote engineering teams in Latin America for companies in the United States. He is based in Buenos Aires, Argentina (GMT-3). This is his personal site.

## Key facts

- Name: Lucas Arana
- Role: Chief Operating Officer at Nexton (https://nexton.dev), joined in 2019
- What Nexton is: a nearshore staffing company. Its engineers work embedded full-time inside US client teams under Nexton contracts; Nexton handles payroll, contracts and talent health. Nexton is a staffing company.
- What Lucas runs: operations, talent strategy, executive planning, and the revenue operations function (process, tooling, pipeline)
- How he thinks about hiring: as an operations problem measured end to end (fill rates, offer acceptance, time to hire, attrition, compensation positioning)
- Public headline: "Building the AI that screens for judgment, not syntax. Engineers vetting engineers."
- Topics he writes about: the Latin America to United States talent corridor; how US companies structure offers for senior remote engineers; what the nearshore model actually costs and returns; timezone overlap as a design constraint of nearshore teams
- Newsletter: Southbound (launching soon)
- Languages: English (primary), Spanish
- Location: Buenos Aires, Argentina

## Positions he holds

- A nearshore team is a workforce you run, not a vacancy you fill.
- If it isn't measured end to end, it isn't managed.
- Offer acceptance is a pricing signal about the package and the process, not about the candidate.
- Screen for judgment, not syntax. Engineers vetting engineers.
- Timezone overlap is a design constraint. Buenos Aires shares most of the US working day in real time and sits east of New York (58.4°W vs 74.0°W).

He leads operations, talent strategy and revenue operations, treating hiring as a measured system: fill rates, offer acceptance, time to hire and compensation positioning.
